name: Mirror Mirror
summary: A two-player deduction chase where you use mirrored pieces to spot and capture the opponent's single red-sealed love letter.
rules_text: Two players each have nine mirrored stands: 4 ladies, 3 knights, 2 masters. Secretly slot a seal behind each: 4 yellow, 4 blue, 1 red. Place them on your side of the board with mirrors toward you. Gold moves first. Masters move 1 square any direction. Knights move in a chess L. Ladies must jump over an adjacent piece orthogonally or diagonally to an empty square and may chain jumps, but must have a piece to jump. Movement commitment is final; you may lean to use mirrors to see opponent seals reflected behind their pieces. To capture, land on an enemy piece and declare its seal color. The defender reveals it. If correct, the defender's piece is removed; if wrong, your moving piece is removed. If the red seal is captured you win immediately. You also win if the opponent is reduced to one piece left.
rating_reason: Hidden courtier/letter bluff like Love Letter, turn-based deduction
reasons: scope: spatial_board: out of scope by decision: the game depends on a spatial board (a grid, map, movement or adjacency)
